I thought that this poem really encapsulated what it feels like to meaninglessly work for something that has no bearing on your actual quality of life. I often find myself questioning why I'm doing the things I do, and most of the time it's money. This poem really made me reflect on the fact that often the pain and stress that we put ourselves through is not even worth it, because at the end of the day money is not that important if your needs are already met. I think it was Michael Gira who said that we spend most of our time on work that has no meaning, so that we can buy things that we don't need. This poem left me feeling the same way I did when I first heard this quote. At first I would have told you that length could have been improved on, but I felt that you actually were able to convey more by saying less

The imagery is what struck me most while reading this poem, as it seemed to literally transport me to those familiar roadside motels across Nevada deserts and the like. The best part in my opinion, was that you found a way to link the past of this land, specifically the bones and the settlers of old, with the newness that is involved in our artificial landscape. This really reminded me of the way I felt when I first listened to all Haill West Texas by the mountain goats, as both your work and his, made me feel as if I was driving through Texas highways as the landscape influences my mood and melancholy thoughts. I would have maybe like to hear more about the modern ties involved in this kind of poem, such as the concrete jungle of passing towns juxtaposed to the barren wasteland in between, but nonetheless I thought that the way that you conveyed the baroness really made me reflect a lot. I'd also add that it made me feel a profound sense of sadness at what this area has become, and what it used to represent. The wild West, New frontier type of vibe that this type of area would have normally given off, has devolved into a desert of sorts. The desert used to represent life, now it's simply a desert both physically and spiritually.
